title: Rainforest Plants
keyIdea: A rainforest has a huge variety of plants, and each is suited to life in a hot, wet, shady forest. Under the treetops it is dark, so plants find ways to reach the light. Giant trees such as the kapok and the Brazil nut tree grow taller than the rest. Lianas are vines that root in the ground and climb up trees. Many orchids grow high on branches with no soil, and their roots soak up rain. Lots of leaves have pointed drip tips that shed the rain, and the giant water lily has round leaves that float on the river.
familyTip: Look at house plants or park plants together. Find a climber (ivy or a bean plant), a plant with a pointed leaf tip, and a tall tree. Pour a little water on a pointed leaf and a round leaf and watch which one drips dry first. Ask: which of these would win the race to the light?

visual.caption: How does each plant get what it needs? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: A kapok grows taller than the other trees
A leaf has a long pointed drip tip
A liana climbs up a tree trunk
An orchid's roots soak up rain from the air
A Brazil nut tree pokes out above the treetops
A water lily leaf floats on the river

lab.caption: Flagship lab: grow a kapok up to the sun, climb a liana up a tree, find an orchid a home, make a drip tip and match five plants.

kid: A rainforest is full of plants. There are giant trees, vines, flowers and huge leaves. The treetops make a thick roof, so the forest floor is dark. Plants need light to grow, so they find ways to get up to it.
Some trees grow very tall. The kapok tree is a giant. It pokes out above all the other trees into the sun. The Brazil nut tree is tall too. Its nuts grow in a hard, round shell as big as a ball.

A liana is a vine with a thin, bendy stem. Its roots are in the ground. It climbs up a tree to reach the light. An orchid is a flower that can grow on a branch, with no soil. Its roots hold on to the bark and soak up rain. It does not hurt the tree.

It rains almost every day. Many leaves have a long pointy tip, called a drip tip. The rain runs off it, so the leaf dries fast. On the river, the giant water lily has a round leaf that floats. It can be wider than a bed is long.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. This supports Year 1 plants in the National Curriculum in England (identify and name a variety of common plants, including trees) and Year 2 living things and their habitats (most living things live in habitats to which they are suited). It builds on What Is a Rainforest? and Rainforest Layers. Key words: plant, tree, trunk, roots, leaf, vine, climber, liana, orchid, drip tip, habitat, sunlight, suited.

Facts used: kapok trees (Ceiba pentandra) are emergents that can reach about 60 metres; Brazil nut trees reach about 50 metres, and each woody fruit, about the size of a coconut, holds 10 to 25 seeds. Lianas are woody climbers rooted in the soil. Many tropical orchids are epiphytes: they grow on other plants for support and take water from rain and moist air, so they are not parasites. Only about 2 per cent of the sunlight reaches the floor of a dense rainforest. Drip tips shed water quickly, which helps keep moss and mould off leaves. Giant water lily (Victoria) leaves grow up to about 3 metres across.

Common mistakes: thinking every plant needs soil to live; thinking trees grow tall to escape animals, or that rain pulls them up; thinking the rainforest floor is bright and sunny; thinking an orchid on a branch feeds on the tree; and thinking a pointed leaf tip is for poking or catching insects. Children may also think lianas grow down from the treetops; the ones here root in the ground.

In the lab your child grows a kapok from the dark floor into full sun, climbs a liana up a trunk (and sees it flop with no tree), finds an orchid a home on a high branch, lengthens a leaf tip until rain runs off, and matches five clues to the kapok, liana, orchid, giant water lily and Brazil nut tree.

practice.prompt: Why is the rainforest floor so dark?
choices: The treetops block most of the light
practice.hint: Look up. What is above the floor?
practice.explain: The treetops make a thick roof of leaves, so very little sunlight reaches the floor.

practice.prompt: An orchid has {a} flowers on a branch. Then {b} more open. How many flowers now?
How does a liana reach the sunlight?
practice.hint: A liana has a thin, bendy stem. What could it hold on to?
practice.explain: A liana roots in the ground and climbs up a tree to get to the light.

practice.prompt: There are {a} leaves with drip tips. Rain runs off {b} of them so far. How many leaves still have rain on them?
practice.hint: Start with {a} leaves. Take away the {b} that are dry.
practice.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b}. {=a-b} leaves are still wet, but the rain will soon run off them too.

practice.prompt: An orchid grows on a branch, with no soil. How does it get water?
practice.hint: It rains almost every day in a rainforest.
practice.explain: The orchid's roots hold on to the bark and soak up rain. It does not hurt the tree.

pool.prompt: Which plant is a giant tree that pokes out above the others?
pool.hint: Look for the plant with a tall trunk whose leafy top is higher than all the other treetops.
pool.explain: The kapok is one of the tallest rainforest trees. It grows above the treetops into full sun.

pool.prompt: Why do rainforest trees grow so tall?
pool.hint: What do plants need to grow that is hard to get on the floor?
pool.explain: Plants need light. Tall trees get their leaves up into the sun above the others.

choices: A vine that climbs up trees
pool.hint: Think of the plant that wound up the trunk in the lab.
pool.explain: A liana is a climbing vine. It roots in the ground and climbs trees to reach the light.

pool.prompt: What is a drip tip for?
choices: Letting rain run off the leaf
pool.explain: Rain runs along the leaf to the pointed tip and drips off, so the leaf dries fast.

pool.prompt: A liana climbs {a} trees. A second liana climbs {b} trees. How many trees is that in all?
pool.hint: Put the two groups of trees together and count them all.

pool.prompt: Where does the giant water lily grow?
pool.hint: Its big round leaf lies flat on the water.
pool.explain: The giant water lily grows in rivers and pools. Its huge round leaves float.

pool.prompt: Mia says every plant must grow in soil. What is right?
choices: Some, like orchids, grow on branches
pool.hint: Think of the orchid in the lab.
pool.explain: Many rainforest orchids grow on branches with no soil. Their roots soak up rain.

pool.prompt: A Brazil nut shell has {a} nuts inside. A hungry agouti takes {b} of them. How many nuts are left in the shell?
pool.hint: Start with all {a} nuts and take away the {b} the agouti took.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b}. {=a-b} nuts are left in the shell.

pool.prompt: What grows inside a hard, round shell on a tall tree?
pool.hint: You may have eaten these nuts.
pool.explain: Brazil nuts grow inside a hard, round shell on the tall Brazil nut tree.
